headline_findings: India's wearables contract-manufacturing base is concentrated in Noida (Dixon Technologies, incl. its 50:50 JV with boAt for wireless audio + smartwatches, Dixon plant B-14/15 Phase-II Noida; Optiemus Electronics with two Noida plants that design AND manufacture hearables/wearables for Noise and Harman) and Manesar (VVDN: 7 of its 9 plants there, with in-house SMT, injection molding, tooling, HPDC and FATP, offered as ODM). [verified: boAt/Dixon JV release + NSE filing; VVDN company site; secondary: trade press on Optiemus]

No standalone wearables/hearables PLI was found to have been notified; the 2021-22 proposals (industry ask of 7-8% incentive, target of ~25% of global wearables output, USD 15-20B production over 4-5 years, notification targeted for 1 Apr 2022) appear to have been superseded by the Budget-2022 Phased Manufacturing Programme, which sets 20% BCD on finished smartwatches/TWS and steps component duty 0-15% across FY23-FY26 with most components at nil from 1 Apr 2022. [secondary: Business Standard 1 Feb 2022, KNN India, Deccan Herald; estimate on PLI status]

The Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme (ECMS) - Cabinet approval 28 Mar 2025, notified 8 Apr 2025, outlay Rs 22,919 crore (~USD 2.7B), 6-year tenure plus optional 1-year gestation - pays incentives tied to factory turnover and employment rather than PLI-style incremental production; targets Rs 59,350 crore investment and 91,600 direct jobs; 31 proposals worth Rs 7,877 crore were cleared as of 17 Aug 2026. [verified: PIB release exists (PRID 2222519); secondary: Manorama Yearbook, Business Standard, ThePrint]

Regulatory floor to sell a BLE wearable in India: BIS CRS on the device under IS 13252 (Part 1):2010 (migrating to IS/IEC 62368-1:2023, deadline 1 Nov 2028 for most products), BIS CRS on the secondary Li-ion cell/battery under IS 16046 (Part 2):2018 (CRS Order 2021), and WPC Equipment Type Approval by self-declaration on DoT's Saral Sanchar portal at Rs 10,000 per product (1-3 working days). [secondary: certification consultancies; the DoT eServices ETA page is the official channel]

Ultrahuman is the only India-headquartered wearables brand found with a disclosed vertically integrated factory model: its Plano, Texas UltraFactory (with EMS partner SVtronics, operational since Nov 2024, targeting 100% of US Ring AIR demand and >500,000 units/yr) is explicitly modelled on its first India facility; Indore-specific capacity, output and unit costs were NOT retrievable this session. [verified: Ultrahuman press releases; Indore figures: not found]

Ultrahuman's own stated reason for bringing manufacturing in-house was COVID-era China volatility plus chip shortages that left consignments stuck for months; the India+US footprint is credited with fewer stockouts and lower import cost/delay. [secondary/blog: Blume VC commentary, ajuniorvc case study]

IP risk is concrete for any ring/band newcomer: the ITC's final determination (announced 9 Sep 2025) found Ultrahuman (India) and RingConn (China) infringed Oura's patent on the arrangement of internal components in a smart ring; exclusion and cease-and-desist orders became effective 21 Oct 2025 after Presidential review; RingConn settled with a multi-year royalty-bearing license, Ultrahuman lost its bids to stay the order and announced a redesigned ring. [verified: Businesswire/Oura release; secondary: Law360, Forbes, Gadgets & Wearables]

The only BoM-structure datapoint retrievable: PCBA is commonly cited as ~40% of an electronic device's bill of materials; components for wearables (PPG/IMU/BLE silicon, cells) are the categories ECMS explicitly flags as import-dependent. [blog-grade: QueenEMS; secondary: ECMS coverage]

NOT FOUND this session (shared WebSearch budget of 200 calls was exhausted after 12 queries in this lens; WebFetch egress-blocked for PIB and KNN): per-unit India EMS SMT + box-build quotes at 5k/25k/100k, injection-mold and test-jig NRE, MOQ and lead times, IDC/Counterpoint 2023-2025 India shipment and locally-made shares, Indian fitness-band ASPs, local value-add %, AT&S/Shogini PCB status, battery-cell localisation, US tariff rate on India-origin goods 2025-26, FCC/CE lab options in India, IEC/GST/DGFT mechanics. Exact follow-up queries are listed in open_questions. [not found]

FX: every USD figure in this file uses Rs 85 per USD, the rate implied by secondary coverage converting the ECMS Rs 22,919 crore outlay to ~USD 2.7 billion (Aug 2026); this sits inside the Rs 83-90 band the prompt anticipated. [estimate]

detailed_notes:
# India contract manufacturing for a screenless strength-training + 24/7 health band — lens notes

**Coverage caveat (read first).** This lens was allotted the project's shared WebSearch budget; it was exhausted (200/200 session calls) after 12 queries in this lens, and both permitted WebFetch attempts (PIB ECMS release; KNN India PMP article) were egress-blocked. Everything below is drawn only from the search-result snippets actually seen. Sections 3, 4, 5 and most of 7 are therefore thin and are flagged NOT FOUND with the exact queries to re-run. No number has been filled from memory. FX used throughout: Rs 85/USD (implied by secondary coverage converting ECMS Rs 22,919 crore to ~USD 2.7 B, Aug 2026; estimate).

## 1. Who actually builds wearables in India

**Dixon Technologies (Noida) — EMS, plus 50:50 JV with boAt.** boAt and Dixon formed a 50-50 joint venture to design and manufacture wireless audio products and smartwatches; output comes from Dixon's facility at B-14 & 15, Phase-II, Noida (verified: boAt newsroom release; Dixon NSE announcement PDF dated 18 Jan 2022). Dixon was already manufacturing wearables for boAt in the fiscal year before the JV, i.e., an EMS (build-to-print) relationship preceded the JV. boAt's stated motivation was the then-proposed PLI for wearables. Dixon's FY22 revenue scale was ~Rs 10,700 crore (~USD 1.26 B) per Forbes India (secondary; current revenue is higher, not retrieved). Model: EMS at scale for large brands; the JV suggests Dixon takes equity stakes with anchor customers rather than running an open ODM catalogue. Fit for a 5k-25k-unit newcomer: unclear; Dixon's known wearables work is brand-anchored, high-volume.

**Optiemus Electronics Ltd (OEL, Noida) — ODM/EMS for hearables & wearables.** Trade press (MyMobile India, Mobility India, Startup Story; c. 2022) reports OEL 'will design and manufacture' hearables for Noise at its two Noida plants; phase one was Make-in-India TWS earbuds with ~6 Noise products planned within 6 months. OEL states 14 M+ mobile devices delivered since 2016 and lists hearable & wearable technology as a service line; named customers include Noise and Harman, and a 2025 Ai+ Smartphone deal (~3 M devices incl. wearables/IoT) (secondary). The 'design and manufacture' language makes OEL the clearest ODM-capable candidate found for a band, alongside VVDN.

**VVDN Technologies (Manesar) — ODM + EMS.** Company site (verified as company-stated): 9 plants — 7 in Manesar, 1 Pollachi, 1 Vizag — with automated SMT, product assembly, mechanical tooling, injection molding, sheet metal, paint shop, powder coating, HPDC, reliability/environmental labs and FATP; explicitly markets concept-to-market ODM. No wearable-specific product line was visible in the snippet, but VVDN's in-house tooling + molding + labs is exactly the stack a strap/band needs (mold tooling can be bought from the EMS itself rather than a separate toolmaker).

**Syrma SGS, Kaynes Technology (listed EMS).** Search results (BusinessToday 17 Feb 2026 on YES Securities' EMS coverage; Syrma corporate site; MarketScreener on MSI laptops at Syrma) contained no wearables/smartwatch programme for either. Both are PCB-assembly/box-build EMS players serving industrial, auto, medical, IT hardware. Annual reports were not retrieved. Treat as 'possible EMS quote sources, no wearables track record found'.

**Not researched (budget):** Amber, Padget (Dixon subsidiary), Jabil India, Flex India, Bharat FIH/Foxconn, Sahasra, Fire-Boltt, Titan/Fastrack, Pebble, Zebronics. No claims made.

**Ultrahuman (brand with own factories) — see section 6.**

## 2. Government schemes and their real economics

**Wearables/hearables PLI — appears never notified.** Coverage from Jan 2021 (Editorji) and 2022 (Business Journal, EFY) describes a scheme 'in the works': target of ~25% of global wearables/hearables output, USD 15-20 B production over 4-5 years, industry ask of 7-8% incentive, notification targeted for 1 Apr 2022 (secondary). No result showed a notified scheme, beneficiary list or rate. MeitY's PLI 2.0 for IT Hardware (applications invited 2023, PIB PRID 1928326) is an IT-hardware scheme. Inference (estimate): the wearables instrument became the customs-duty ladder (PMP), not a cash PLI. A newcomer should assume **no production subsidy** for a band assembled in India unless it qualifies as a component maker under ECMS.

**Phased Manufacturing Programme (PMP) for wrist wearables, hearables, smart meters — Budget 1 Feb 2022.** Business Standard / KNN India / Deccan Herald (secondary): BCD on imported finished smartwatches, TWS, headphones, neckbands set at 20%; component duty 0-15% between FY23 and FY26 with most components at nil from 1 Apr 2022 and rising in steps. The per-item ladder (PCBA, charger, battery/cell, display assembly, mechanics) by fiscal year and the CBIC notification number were not retrieved (page blocked). Economic logic: finished-good import is penalised (~20% BCD plus SWS/IGST — additional levies not confirmed in snippets), CKD/SKD assembly is cheap early, and sub-assembly duties escalate to push PCBA population and cell packing onshore. Post-FY26 status (i.e., what applies in FY27, now) NOT retrieved — a key open item.

**ECMS (Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme).** Cabinet-approved 28 Mar 2025, notified 8 Apr 2025, outlay Rs 22,919 crore (~USD 2.7 B), 6-year tenure plus optional 1-year gestation (verified: PIB page exists; details via Manorama Yearbook 18 Aug 2026 and News On AIR). Incentives are linked to factory turnover and employment (not incremental production), across components, sub-assemblies, capital equipment and supply-chain products flagged as import-dependent. Targets: Rs 59,350 crore (~USD 6.98 B) investment, 91,600 direct jobs. As of 17 Aug 2026, 31 proposals worth Rs 7,877 crore (~USD 927 M) were cleared (Business Standard, ThePrint). Per-category incentive percentages, capex-subsidy shares and minimum-investment thresholds were NOT retrieved. Relevance: a band brand is a *user* of ECMS-supported components (cells, PCBs, sensors), not a beneficiary.

**SPECS:** not researched (budget).

**BIS CRS.** Device: IS 13252 (Part 1):2010 registration is mandatory before sale or import of smartwatches (consultancy sources: EVTL, ASC, Diligence, Elitas, ERA Global; secondary). Battery: every portable device powered by a secondary lithium cell needs IS 16046 (Part 2):2018 CRS registration under the 2021 CRS Order (Standphill; secondary) — so an imported Chinese cell/pack must be BIS-registered (by cell maker or importer) before the band ships in India. Transition: IS/IEC 62368-1:2023 replaces IS 13252 and IS 616, migration deadline 1 Nov 2028 for most products (Elitas, 2026; secondary — verify against gazette). BIS test/registration fees and lab lead-times NOT retrieved.

**WPC ETA.** The DoT eServices portal hosts Equipment Type Approval (verified page exists). For de-licensed bands (Bluetooth 2.4 GHz, Wi-Fi, Zigbee, RFID) the self-declaration route (ETA-SD) runs on Saral Sanchar; fee Rs 10,000 (~USD 118) per product with one or more RF modules; 1-3 working days once an RF test report is in hand (Standphill, SIACC 2026, Seyecs 2026, Granite River Labs; secondary).

**Import duty on finished wearables vs SKD/CKD:** 20% BCD on finished (secondary); SKD/CKD rates by line item NOT retrieved.

## 3. Local ecosystem depth

NOT FOUND for AT&S Nanjangud, Shogini, cell localisation, and any Counterpoint/IDC/ICEA local-value-add %. What the retrieved material supports: (a) SMT, injection molding, tooling, paint/coating, sheet-metal and FATP exist in-house at VVDN (verified) and design+build at OEL (secondary), so *conversion* is fully local; (b) ECMS is explicitly built around import-dependent components/sub-assemblies, consistent with silicon (PPG/IMU/BLE SoC), cells and displays being imported; (c) generic blog-grade figure: PCBA ~40% of BoM (QueenEMS) — for a screenless band with no display, the PCBA share is plausibly higher (unsourced). No local value-add percentage is asserted.

## 4. Actual cost quotes / indications

NOT FOUND. No sourced per-unit SMT + box-build quote at 5k/25k/100k units, no injection-mold or test-jig NRE, MOQ or lead-time figures were retrieved. Per the no-fabrication rule none are estimated here. Related facts only: WPC ETA Rs 10,000/product; VVDN/OEL can supply mold tooling in-house. Queries to run are in open_questions.

## 5. Market data

NOT FOUND for IDC/Counterpoint India shipments 2023-2025, locally-made share, and band ASPs. Only dated planning figures surfaced: global wearables market USD 25-30 B (2021-22) expected to reach USD 80-85 B in 4-5 years (Business Journal; secondary, stale).

## 6. Ultrahuman case study

- **Factory model.** Ultrahuman's US UltraFactory in Plano, Texas, run with EMS partner SVtronics, has been operational since Nov 2024, aims to serve 100% of US Ring AIR demand and to scale to >500,000 units/yr; the company states it is based on its first operational UltraFactory in India (verified: company press releases). A further Indiana plant is planned (Inside Indiana Business; secondary). A USD 35 M round accompanied the US expansion (Citeline; secondary). **Indore-specific capacity, output, headcount and unit cost: NOT FOUND** — the prompt's premise (Indore, 2023) was not independently confirmed.
- **Why in-house / why India.** Investor and analyst blogs (Blume VC commentary; ajuniorvc case study; both secondary/partisan) say COVID-era China volatility and chip shortages left consignments stuck for months, prompting in-house manufacturing; the India+US footprint is credited with fewer stockouts and lower import cost/delay. The specific Shenzhen-to-India move narrative was not found in a primary source.
- **Scale.** A blog title puts Ultrahuman at ~Rs 1,000 crore (~USD 118 M) (ajuniorvc; blog-grade). Ring AIR price, subscription-free model and unit economics: NOT retrieved (the Ultrahuman India buy page appeared in results but was not fetched). Business Standard (5 Nov 2025) reports the CEO saying Ultrahuman will 'relaunch in India with more products soon' — implying an earlier India pull-back, reason not retrieved.
- **IP lesson.** ITC final determination announced 9 Sep 2025: Ultrahuman and RingConn infringed Oura's patent covering how internal components are arranged inside a smart ring; exclusion and cease-and-desist orders took effect 21 Oct 2025 after Presidential review (verified: Businesswire, Oura blog; Law360). RingConn settled with a multi-year royalty-bearing license; Ultrahuman lost bids to stay the order and announced continued support plus a redesigned ring (Law360; Gadgets & Wearables 22 Oct 2025). Takeaway for a band: the winning patent was a *mechanical packaging* claim, not an algorithm — freedom-to-operate on form-factor/packaging patents (Whoop, Oura, Fitbit/Google, Apple) must precede tooling, and an India-built product is still fully exposed at the US border via Section 337.

## 7. Practical playbook for a small US-based founder

Retrieved facts: (i) Indian EMS/ODM engagement is possible without a JV — OEL designs+builds for brands, VVDN offers ODM; (ii) India sale requires BIS CRS (device + cell) and WPC ETA-SD (Rs 10,000/product, days); (iii) India-side exit for US export would face whatever US tariff applies to India-origin goods — **rate NOT retrieved; must be checked against Federal Register/USTR/CBP before any landed-cost model.** NOT retrieved: IEC/GST/DGFT registration mechanics, whether an Indian entity is needed vs contract-only, FCC/CE labs in India (TUV SUD, UL Bengaluru, STQC) and their pricing. Granite River Labs surfaced as a lab with an India market-access practice (secondary).

## What is solid enough to model now

1. Regulatory fixed costs for India sale: WPC ETA Rs 10,000/product (secondary) + BIS CRS device and battery (fees not found).
2. Import-duty asymmetry: 20% BCD on finished wearables vs 0-15% components (FY23-26; secondary) — local assembly is duty-advantaged inside India; irrelevant for US-bound export except as a hint that CKD import into India is cheap.
3. Candidate partners: OEL (Noida, ODM+EMS, hearables/wearables track record), VVDN (Manesar, ODM+EMS, full mechanical stack), Dixon (Noida, EMS at scale, brand-anchored).
4. IP: Section 337 exclusion is a live precedent (Oct 2025) for India-built rings.

Everything else in this lens is an open question.
